questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of an animal cell as seen under the electron microscope. *(7 marks)*

State the functions of the following parts of the cell:

(i) Mitochondrion

(ii) Cell membrane

(iii) Nucleus. *(2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Mitochondrion**: the site of **aerobic respiration**, where glucose is oxidised to release **energy** stored as **ATP** for the activities of the cell.

(ii) **Cell membrane**: **controls the passage of substances into and out of the cell** (it is selectively permeable) and holds the contents of the cell together.

(iii) **Nucleus**: **controls all the activities of the cell** and contains the **chromosomes (DNA)** that carry the hereditary information; it is necessary for cell division.

questions.enonce_markdown: In tabular form state the differences between mitosis and meiosis. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Mitosis | Meiosis |
|---|---|
| Produces **two** daughter cells | Produces **four** daughter cells |
| Daughter cells have the **same chromosome number (diploid, $2n$)** as the parent cell | Daughter cells have **half the chromosome number (haploid, $n$)** |
| One division only | **Two** successive divisions (meiosis I and II) |
| Daughter cells are **genetically identical** to the parent cell | Daughter cells are **genetically different** (variation) |
| No pairing of homologous chromosomes | **Homologous chromosomes pair up** (bivalents) |
| No crossing over | **Crossing over** (exchange of segments) occurs between chromatids |
| Occurs in body (somatic) cells, for growth, repair and asexual reproduction | Occurs in the reproductive organs (testes, ovaries), to form **gametes** |
